title: The roots-of-unity filter, first non-real case
content: The parent combinations-formula-oq-05 splits a Pascal row by parity: even- and odd-indexed binomial coefficients each sum to 2^{n-1}. That is the mod-2 instance of a general phenomenon — for any modulus m, the residue-class sum S_r of C(n,k) over indices k ≡ r (mod m) is extracted from (1+x)^n by averaging its values at the m-th roots of unity (the roots-of-unity / finite Fourier filter). This file formalizes m = 3, the first case where the roots of unity are genuinely complex: a primitive cube root ω = e^{2πi/3} is unavoidable, unlike the parent's real ±1 evaluation.

title: Fixing a primitive cube root and its basic laws
content: ω is fixed as Complex.exp(2πi/3), certified a primitive cube root of unity via Complex.isPrimitiveRoot_exp. Three consequences are drawn directly from the IsPrimitiveRoot API: ω³ = 1 (pow_eq_one), ω ≠ 1 (ne_one), and the general divisibility criterion ω^m = 1 ⟺ 3 ∣ m (pow_eq_one_iff_dvd). The last fact is what later turns a complex-exponent identity into the purely arithmetic residue condition k % 3 = r.

title: Cube roots annihilate 1 + t + t²
content: cube_root_sum: for any t with t³ = 1 and t ≠ 1, necessarily 1 + t + t² = 0. The proof factors (t − 1)(1 + t + t²) = t³ − 1 = 0 by `ring` + the hypothesis, then splits on `mul_eq_zero`: since t ≠ 1 rules out the first factor, the second must vanish. Note the hypothesis is only t³ = 1, not that t is a *primitive* cube root — the lemma applies to every power ω^m appearing later, not just ω itself.
prerequisites: ℂ is a field (no zero divisors)

title: Roots-of-unity filter modulo 3
content: filter3: ∑_{j<3} ω^{jm} equals 3 when 3 ∣ m, and 0 otherwise. The sum is unrolled to its three literal terms (sum_range_succ ×3). When 3 ∣ m, write m = 3c: both ω^{3c} and ω^{2·3c} reduce to 1 via ω³ = 1, so the three terms are 1+1+1 = 3. Off the divisibility locus, ω^m is itself a cube root of unity (from ω³ = 1) distinct from 1 (from ω_pow_eq_one_iff), so cube_root_sum applies directly to t = ω^m and gives 0.

title: The three-way extraction identity (main result)
content: three_way_split, the heart of the answer to OQ-05-OQ-02: for r < 3, 3·S_r(n) = ∑_{j<3} ω^{2jr}(1+ω^j)^n. The calc proof (1) expands each (1+ω^j)^n binomially via add_pow, (2) swaps the j- and k-sums with Finset.sum_comm to isolate, for each fixed k, the inner sum ∑_j ω^{j(k+2r)}, (3) collapses that inner sum through filter3 — it is 3·C(n,k) exactly when 3 ∣ (k+2r), i.e. when k % 3 = r, a translation discharged uniformly by `omega`, and (4) reassembles the surviving terms into 3·S_r(n) via Finset.sum_filter. All exponents stay natural-number valued (ω^{-jr} is encoded as ω^{2jr} since ω^{3j} = 1, i.e. ω^{-1} = ω²), so the whole extraction is Finset bookkeeping with no complex-analytic machinery beyond ω³ = 1.

title: Dual (generating) identity
content: dual_identity: S_0(n) + ω·S_1(n) + ω²·S_2(n) = (1+ω)^n. Unlike three_way_split, which recovers each class separately, this packages all three residue-class sums into a single complex evaluation of the generating function at ω. The proof expands (1+ω)^n binomially into ∑_k C(n,k)ω^k, rewrites each S_r as an indicator sum, uses ω^k = ω^{k mod 3} (from ω³ = 1) to fold every term into one of the three residue classes, and matches coefficients termwise by casing on k % 3 ∈ {0,1,2}.

title: Partition check: the three classes recover the full row
content: sum_three_residues: S_0(n) + S_1(n) + S_2(n) = 2^n. A sanity check that the three residue classes mod 3 genuinely partition row n: rewriting each S_r as an indicator sum and combining, every k ∈ range(n+1) contributes to exactly one of the three cases (k % 3 = 0, 1, or 2), so the combined sum matches Nat.sum_range_choose = 2^n termwise. Confirms no coefficient is double-counted or dropped by the extraction machinery.
